2. The short facts necessary for disposal of this review application are that this petitioner while he was working as bench assistant in the labour court, Rajshahi a departmental proceeding was started against him by framing charges on 24.04.1987 and in that departmental proceeding, after necessary inquiry as per rules, the petitioner was found guilty of the charges and the punishment of compulsory retirement was awarded against him by the order dated 17.08.1987. The petitioner preferred a departmental appeal against that order on 11.10.1987 which was rejected on 02.05.1988. The petitioner then filed a revision to the Hon'ble President on 11.11.1988 which was also rejected on 09.03.2000. The petitioner thereafter filed Administrative Tribunal Case No. 62 of 2000 before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra for setting aside the said order of compulsory retirement. The opposite party contested the said A.T. case by filing written statement. The material defence case of this contesting respondent was that A.T. case was barred by limitation and as such liable to be dismissed. The Administrative Tribunal, Bogra, after hearing both the parties, dismissed that A.T case on the ground of limitation. 

 3. Being aggrieved by that judgment and order of the Administrative Tribunal this petitioner filed appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal also, after hearing the petitioner, found the case barred by limitation and dismissed the appeal. The petitioner thereafter filed the above mentioned Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 529 of 2008 before this Division. This Division, after hearing the learned Counsel of the petitioner and perusing the leave petition and the , impugned judgments of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal and also of the Administrative Tribunal dismissed the said leave petition holding that the Administrative Tribunal case was barred by limitation. 

 5. It appears that both the Administrative Tribunal and the Administrative Appellate Tribunal found that the original Administrative Tribunal case was filed beyond the statutory period of limitation and as such was not maintainable. This Division also considered this point of limitation and found that the Administrative Tribunal case was barred by limitation. So we find no ground at all for reviewing the judgment and order of this Division. There is no mistake or error apparent on the face of record or any other grounds mentioned in Order 47, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure for reviewing the judgment and order sought to be reviewed.
